summary: Lists the situations where DNS, protected by DNSSEC, could help a client decide whether a TLS server is really the one it claims to be. Today that job is mostly done by certificate authorities, and the DNS could add extra assertions. This informational document gathers the use cases and requirements that led to the DANE work.

eli5.summary: When you visit a website, your computer wants proof it is the right one. Right now it asks trusted certificate-givers. This note imagines also checking the internet's phone book, so there is a second way to confirm.

questions: use dnssec to authenticate tls servers
